title: Drinking water disinfectant residuals and byproducts practice questions
description: Free practice questions on 40 CFR 141 Subpart L: disinfectant residuals, DBP monitoring, compliance and TOC removal, each linked to the rule.

questions.topic: Who Subpart L covers and when
questions.question: Under 141.130(a)(2), which transient noncommunity water systems must modify their practices to meet a Subpart L requirement?

options.A: Every transient noncommunity system that adds any chemical disinfectant
options.B: Those that use chlorine dioxide as a disinfectant or oxidant
options.C: Those that use ozone for disinfection
options.D: Those that use chloramines to maintain a distribution system residual

questions.explanation: Subpart L covers "transient NCWSs that use chlorine dioxide as a disinfectant or oxidant", which "must modify their practices to meet the MRDL for chlorine dioxide in § 141.65." The wider coverage in 141.130(a)(1) is for CWSs and NTNCWSs.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.130, General requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who Subpart L covers and when
questions.question: What does 141.130(c) require of the people who operate a CWS or NTNCWS regulated under Subpart L?

options.A: They must hold an operator certificate issued by EPA
options.B: They must complete an EPA-approved disinfection course every three years
options.C: They must be employees of a State-certified laboratory
options.D: They must be qualified personnel who meet State requirements and are on a State register of qualified operators

questions.explanation: Each such system "must be operated by qualified personnel who meet the requirements specified by the State and are included in a State register of qualified operators."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.130, General requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who Subpart L covers and when
questions.question: According to 141.64(b)(1)(i), until when must systems comply with the Subpart L (running annual average) MCLs for TTHM and HAA5?

options.A: Until the date specified for subpart V compliance in 141.620(c)
options.B: Until January 1, 2004
options.C: Until the State approves the system's monitoring plan
options.D: Until the system qualifies for reduced monitoring

questions.explanation: 141.64(b)(1)(i) states: "All systems must comply with these MCLs until the date specified for subpart V compliance in § 141.620(c)." From that date the subpart V MCLs apply as a locational running annual average.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.64, Maximum contaminant levels for disinfection byproducts (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.131(b)(2), who must conduct the analyses for disinfection byproducts, apart from the exception in paragraph (b)(3)?

options.A: Any laboratory that uses an EPA method, certified or not
options.B: The system's own certified operator
options.C: Laboratories that have received certification by EPA or the State
options.D: State drinking water program staff only

questions.explanation: DBP analyses "must be conducted by laboratories that have received certification by EPA or the State, except as specified under paragraph (b)(3) of this section." Paragraph (b)(3) covers daily chlorite samples at the entrance to the distribution system.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.131, Analytical requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When individual trihalomethane results are added to calculate TTHM, what value does the 141.131(b)(2)(iv) table footnote use for a result below the MRL, unless the State specifies otherwise?

options.A: Zero
options.B: The MRL value itself
options.C: Half of the MRL value
options.D: The highest result in the sample batch

questions.explanation: The footnote states that "a zero is used for any analytical result that is less than the MRL concentration for that DBP, unless otherwise specified by the State."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.131, Analytical requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Subpart L routine monitoring table in 141.132(b)(1)(i), a Subpart H system serving fewer than 500 persons takes its one yearly TTHM and HAA5 sample per plant, and the sample exceeds the MCL. What must the system do next?

options.A: Take four samples per quarter per treatment plant at average residence time locations
options.B: Increase monitoring to one sample per treatment plant per quarter at a point reflecting the maximum residence time, until it meets the criteria in 141.132(b)(1)(iv)
options.C: Move to one sample per treatment plant per three-year monitoring cycle
options.D: Stop TTHM and HAA5 sampling until the State's next sanitary survey

questions.explanation: The table says that if the sample exceeds the MCL, "the system must increase monitoring to one sample per treatment plant per quarter, taken at a point reflecting the maximum residence time in the distribution system, until the system meets criteria in paragraph (b)(1)(iv) of this section." Under 141.64(b)(1)(i), the Subpart L TTHM and HAA5 MCLs apply only until the subpart V compliance date.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Subpart L text in 141.132(a)(2), what may a system do with multiple wells drawing water from a single aquifer when determining the minimum number of TTHM and HAA5 samples?

options.A: Leave those wells out of TTHM and HAA5 monitoring
options.B: Sample only the well with the highest flow, without State approval
options.C: Composite one sample from all the wells each year
options.D: Consider them as one treatment plant, with State approval under criteria developed under 142.16(h)(5)

questions.explanation: "Systems may consider multiple wells drawing water from a single aquifer as one treatment plant for determining the minimum number of TTHM and HAA5 samples required, with State approval in accordance with criteria developed under § 142.16(h)(5) of this chapter." This is the Subpart L text; under 141.64(b)(1)(i) the Subpart L TTHM and HAA5 MCLs apply only until the subpart V compliance date.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Subpart L, what "no more than" levels does 141.132(b)(1)(iv) set for TTHMs and HAA5 for a system to remain on a reduced monitoring schedule?

options.A: 0.080 mg/L TTHMs and 0.060 mg/L HAA5
options.B: 0.040 mg/L TTHMs and 0.030 mg/L HAA5
options.C: 0.060 mg/L TTHMs and 0.045 mg/L HAA5
options.D: 0.020 mg/L TTHMs and 0.015 mg/L HAA5

questions.explanation: A system may remain on reduced monitoring as long as its yearly average or single result "is no more than 0.060 mg/L and 0.045 mg/L for TTHMs and HAA5, respectively." The 0.040 and 0.030 mg/L levels are the conditions for qualifying to reduce. Under 141.64(b)(1)(i), the Subpart L TTHM and HAA5 MCLs apply only until the subpart V compliance date.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.132(b)(2)(i)(A), what must a system do when a daily chlorite sample at the entrance to the distribution system exceeds the chlorite MCL?

options.A: Switch from daily to weekly entrance sampling
options.B: Wait for the next monthly three-sample set before taking more samples
options.C: Take one more entrance sample later the same week only
options.D: Take additional distribution system samples the following day at the locations in (b)(2)(ii), in addition to the entrance sample

questions.explanation: "For any daily sample that exceeds the chlorite MCL, the system must take additional samples in the distribution system the following day at the locations required by paragraph (b)(2)(ii) of this section, in addition to the sample required at the entrance to the distribution system."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.132(b)(3)(i), which systems must take routine monthly bromate samples?

options.A: Community and nontransient noncommunity systems using ozone for disinfection or oxidation
options.B: All systems using chlorine dioxide
options.C: Transient noncommunity systems using ozone
options.D: All systems using chloramines

questions.explanation: "Community and nontransient noncommunity systems using ozone, for disinfection or oxidation, must take one sample per month for each treatment plant in the system using ozone."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Beginning April 1, 2016, under 141.132(c)(1)(i), with which sampling must CWSs and NTNCWSs that use chlorine or chloramines match the point and time of their distribution system residual measurements?

options.A: The monthly chlorite three-sample set
options.B: Total coliform sampling under 141.854 through 141.858
options.C: Lead and copper tap sampling
options.D: Quarterly TTHM sampling at maximum residence time locations

questions.explanation: They "must measure the residual disinfectant level in the distribution system at the same point in the distribution system and at the same time as total coliforms are sampled, as specified in §§ 141.854 through 141.858."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: On routine monitoring under 141.132(d)(1), what TOC and alkalinity sampling does a Subpart H system using conventional filtration take for each plant?

options.A: One paired sample and one source water alkalinity sample per quarter
options.B: Four paired samples per quarter and no alkalinity sample
options.C: One paired sample and one source water alkalinity sample per month
options.D: One treated water TOC sample per year during the month of warmest water temperature

questions.explanation: "Systems must take one paired sample and one source water alkalinity sample per month per plant at a time representative of normal operating conditions and influent water quality." Quarterly sampling is the reduced schedule in 141.132(d)(2).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.132(f), which systems must submit a copy of their monitoring plan to the State no later than the date of the first report required under 141.134?

options.A: All Subpart H systems serving more than 3300 people
options.B: Only ground water systems serving fewer than 500 people
options.C: Only transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide
options.D: Only systems that have already had an MCL violation

questions.explanation: "All Subpart H systems serving more than 3300 people must submit a copy of the monitoring plan to the State no later than the date of the first report required under § 141.134." The State may also require any other system to submit its plan.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.132, Monitoring requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.133(a)(2), which samples taken and analyzed under Subpart L must be included in determining compliance?

options.A: Only the minimum number of samples required
options.B: Only samples taken at maximum residence time locations
options.C: Only the samples the State selects
options.D: All of them, even if that number is greater than the minimum required

questions.explanation: "All samples taken and analyzed under the provisions of this subpart must be included in determining compliance, even if that number is greater than the minimum required."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.133, Compliance requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.133(b)(3), on what is compliance with the chlorite MCL based?

options.A: A running annual arithmetic average, computed quarterly, of monthly samples
options.B: An arithmetic average of each three-sample set taken in the distribution system
options.C: Each single daily sample at the entrance to the distribution system
options.D: The highest single distribution system sample in a calendar year

questions.explanation: "Compliance must be based on an arithmetic average of each three sample set taken in the distribution system". A running annual average of monthly samples is the basis for bromate in 141.133(b)(2).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.133, Compliance requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.133(c)(2)(i), which set of chlorine dioxide results is an acute MRDL violation?

options.A: Two consecutive daily entrance samples exceed the MRDL while all distribution system samples are below it
options.B: The running annual average of monthly averages exceeds the MRDL
options.C: A daily entrance sample exceeds the MRDL and, on the following day, one or more of the three distribution system samples exceed it
options.D: One monthly distribution system sample exceeds the MRDL

questions.explanation: "If any daily sample taken at the entrance to the distribution system exceeds the MRDL, and on the following day one (or more) of the three samples taken in the distribution system exceed the MRDL, the system is in violation of the MRDL" and must notify the public under the procedures for acute health risks. Two exceeding entrance samples with all distribution samples below is the nonacute case.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.133, Compliance requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What reporting deadline does 141.134(a) set for a system required to sample quarterly or more frequently?

options.A: 48 hours after each sample is collected
options.B: 10 days after the end of each quarter in which samples were collected
options.C: 30 days after the end of each calendar year
options.D: July 1 of each year, with the Consumer Confidence Report

questions.explanation: These systems "must report to the State within 10 days after the end of each quarter in which samples were collected, notwithstanding the provisions of § 141.31."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.134, Reporting and recordkeeping requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.135(a)(1), which systems must operate with enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening to achieve the required TOC percent removals, unless they meet an alternative compliance criterion?

options.A: Subpart H systems using conventional filtration treatment
options.B: All systems using only ground water that add a disinfectant
options.C: Subpart H systems that do not filter
options.D: Transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide

questions.explanation: "Subpart H systems using conventional filtration treatment (as defined in § 141.2) must operate with enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening" to achieve the TOC removals in 141.135(b), "unless the system meets at least one of the alternative compliance criteria".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.135, Treatment technique for control of disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.135(b)(2), which column of the Step 1 TOC removal table must a Subpart H conventional treatment system practicing softening meet for its source water TOC?

options.A: The 0-60 mg/L source water alkalinity column
options.B: The >60-120 mg/L source water alkalinity column
options.C: A column the system picks again each quarter
options.D: The far-right column (source water alkalinity >120 mg/L)

questions.explanation: "Systems practicing softening are required to meet the Step 1 TOC reductions in the far-right column", and the table's footnote adds: "System practicing softening must meet the TOC removal requirements in this column."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.135, Treatment technique for control of disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What application deadline does 141.135(b)(3) set for a Subpart H conventional treatment system that cannot achieve the Step 1 TOC removals and seeks alternative minimum (Step 2) removal requirements?

options.A: 10 days after the end of the quarter
options.B: One year after its first TOC sample
options.C: Within three months of failure to achieve the Step 1 TOC removals
options.D: 30 days following its compliance date in 141.130(b)

questions.explanation: Such systems "must apply to the State, within three months of failure to achieve the TOC removals required by paragraph (b)(2) of this section". Until the State approves, they "must meet the Step 1 TOC removals".
